sections.title: Listen and read
sections.heading: Medicine for Lucas
sections.scene: Tuesday afternoon. Elif is at the pharmacy on Harbor Street, next to the bank.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Hi. My friend has the flu. He has a fever and a bad cough. What should he take?

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: OK. For the fever, he can take these tablets. They're painkillers too, so they're good for his headache.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: How many tablets should he take?

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Two tablets every six hours. But not more than eight tablets in one day.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: This cough syrup is good. Two teaspoons, three times a day, after meals.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: No, not for these. The syrup is nine fifty, and the tablets are six twenty-five. One more thing: the syrup can make him sleepy, so he shouldn't drive.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Drive? He can't even get out of bed!

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Then he's going to sleep very well. I hope he feels better soon.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: How to read a medicine label
sections.intro: From a health page on the pharmacy's website.
paragraphs: Before you take any medicine, read the label. It tells you four important things.
First: what is it for? For example, "for fever and headache" or "for coughs".
Second: how much should you take? The label tells you how many tablets, or how much syrup. For children, it's usually less.
Third: how often should you take it? "Every six hours" means four times a day. "Twice a day" means in the morning and in the evening.
Fourth: the warnings. Some medicines can make you sleepy, so you shouldn't drive. Some aren't good for people with allergies.
Never take more than the label says. More medicine doesn't make you better faster!
And if you have questions, ask the pharmacist. That's their job, and it's free.

options: in the morning and in the evening

sections.title: Grammar: How much / How many, how often

head: Use with
Example
rows: **once / twice / three times** a day, **every** six hours

rules: Countable nouns have a plural: *tablet → tablets*. Uncountable nouns don't: *water, medicine, syrup, sleep*.
**once** = one time, **twice** = two times, then **three times, four times** …
**every** + number + plural: *every six hours*. But *every day* (singular).
examples: How many hours do you sleep?
How much water do you drink?
Take one tablet twice a day.

support.tr: How many = kaç tane (sayılabilen, çoğul isimlerle: tablets, days). How much = ne kadar (sayılamayan isimlerle: water, syrup) ve fiyat için (How much is it?). Sıklık: once a day = günde bir kez, twice a day = günde iki kez, three times a day = günde üç kez. every six hours = altı saatte bir.
support.ar: How many = كم عدد (مع الأسماء المعدودة الجمع: tablets، days). How much = كم كمية (مع غير المعدودة: water، syrup) وللسعر (How much is it?). التكرار: once a day = مرة في اليوم، twice a day = مرتين في اليوم، three times a day = ثلاث مرات في اليوم. every six hours = كل ست ساعات.

tr.note: How many'den sonra isim çoğul olur; "günde iki kez" = twice a day.
